title: A speech at a wedding: saying less, meaning more
goal: Write and give a short wedding speech in Swedish, using understatement, self-irony and the rituals of the Swedish toast — and look back over the whole Svenska series.
bekal: you can decode and use Swedish understatement: *inte helt hopplös*, *inte illa*, *inte så dum*
you can structure a speech and lead a toast: *Får jag be alla att höja glasen… Skål!*
you can draw on grammar from all four levels — counterfactuals, deponents, passive, word order — in one text
wave: Go back to Unit 15: choose three idioms (for example *ingen ko på isen*, *glida in på en räkmacka*, *inte för fem öre*) and build one of them into a two-sentence toast for a friend.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Generalrepetition
dialogs.intro: A Friday in June, the evening before Elin and Erik's wedding at a manor house outside Stockholm. Elin's brother Jonas is the toastmaster. He finds Dian on the terrace with a sheet of paper, mumbling to herself.

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Som toastmaster måste jag fråga: hur långt är ditt tal?
lines.id: As toastmaster I have to ask: how long is your speech?
lines.literal: as toastmaster must I ask: how long is your speech?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Tre minuter, ungefär. Är det för kort?
lines.id: About three minutes. Is that too short?
lines.literal: three minutes, approximately. is it too short?

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Tvärtom, det är perfekt. Gästerna vill hinna äta medan maten är varm.
lines.id: On the contrary, it's perfect. The guests want to get to eat while the food is hot.
lines.literal: on-the-contrary, it is perfect. guests-the want manage eat while food-the is warm.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Får jag öva på dig? Jag är lite orolig för att skämten inte ska gå hem.
lines.id: Can I practice on you? I'm a bit worried the jokes won't land.
lines.literal: may I practice on you? I am a-little worried for that jokes-the not shall go home.

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Kör. Men en varning: svenskar skrattar mest åt självironi. Skryt inte för mycket om brudparet.
lines.id: Go ahead. But a warning: Swedes laugh most at self-irony. Don't brag too much about the bride and groom.
lines.literal: drive. but a warning: Swedes laugh most at self-irony. brag not too much about bride-couple-the.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Jantelagen, alltså? Man ska inte tro att man är något?
lines.id: Jante's law, you mean? You mustn't think you're anything special?
lines.literal: Jante-law-the, so? one shall not believe that one is something?

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Ungefär. Säg hellre att Erik är "inte helt hopplös" — då förstår alla att du menar att han är fantastisk.
lines.id: More or less. Better to say Erik is "not completely hopeless" — then everyone understands you mean he's wonderful.
lines.literal: approximately. say rather that Erik is "not wholly hopeless" — then understand all that you mean that he is fantastic.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Underdrift som komplimang. Det har jag lärt mig av er under de här åren.
lines.id: Understatement as a compliment. I've learned that from you all over these years.
lines.literal: under-drift as compliment. that have I learned me from you-all during these here years-the.

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Och avsluta med en skål. Alla reser sig, tittar varandra i ögonen, dricker — och tittar i ögonen igen.
lines.id: And finish with a toast. Everyone stands up, looks each other in the eye, drinks — and looks each other in the eye again.
lines.literal: and finish with a toast. all raise themselves, look each-other in eyes-the, drink — and look in eyes-the again.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Och sedan sätter man sig? Eller ska man sjunga först?
lines.id: And then you sit down? Or are you supposed to sing first?
lines.literal: and then set one oneself? or shall one sing first?

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Snapsvisorna kommer senare. Under talen sitter alla tysta — utom pappa, som gråter.
lines.id: The drinking songs come later. During the speeches everyone sits quietly — except Dad, who cries.
lines.literal: schnapps-songs-the come later. during speeches-the sit all quiet — except dad, who cries.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Lars gråter? Det hade jag aldrig trott.
lines.id: Lars cries? I'd never have thought it.
lines.literal: Lars cries? that had I never believed.

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Det tror ingen. Det är därför det är så rörande.
lines.id: Nobody does. That's why it's so moving.
lines.literal: that believes nobody. it is therefore it is so moving.

notes: **Toastmaster** (**TOHST-mahs-ter**) — at a Swedish wedding dinner, a friend or relative (*toastmaster* or *toastmadame*) leads the evening: announces the speeches, keeps time, and tells the guests when to stand and sing. You must **anmäla ditt tal** (register your speech) with the toastmaster in advance — just standing up to speak is considered rude.

**Gå hem** literally "go home": of a joke or message, "to land, to be well received". *Skämtet gick hem* (the joke landed), *budskapet gick inte hem* (the message didn't get through). **Skämt** is pronounced **hwemt** — *sk* before *ä*.

**Jantelagen** (**YAHN-teh-lah-gen**), "the Law of Jante", comes from a 1933 novel by the Danish-Norwegian writer Aksel Sandemose. Its first rule — *Du ska inte tro att du är något* — sums up a Nordic suspicion of boasting. Swedes usually mention it critically, but its spirit shapes how they praise: lightly, and with a wink.

**Underdrift** (**ÜN-der-drift**) = understatement, the opposite of *överdrift* (exaggeration). Saying *inte helt hopplös* about the groom is a compliment precisely because everyone hears the understatement. Delivered with a straight face, it is the heart of Swedish humor.

**Tittar varandra i ögonen** — the Swedish *skål* has a fixed ritual: raise the glass, look at the people near you, drink, and look at them again before putting the glass down. Skipping the eye contact is noticed. *Skål* (**skohl**) originally meant "bowl".

**Det hade jag aldrig trott** — the pluperfect is used here as a softened conditional, "I would never have thought it" (Svenska 103, Unit 14). **Rörande** (**RÖ-rahn-deh**) — moving, touching — is a present participle used as an adjective (Svenska 103, Unit 9).

grammars.title: Saying less to mean more
body: Swedish praise and criticism are often wrapped in understatement (litotes): you deny the opposite instead of stating the thing itself. The table shows how to hear the real message.
after: Irony in Swedish is delivered flat — no wink, no change of tone. *Det tog bara tre år* (it only took three years) works because the speaker says it as if it were a short time.

Self-irony is the safest kind of joke in a Swedish speech: make fun of your own mistakes, never of the couple's. A story about your own failed Swedish is worth more than ten clever jokes about the groom.

dialogs.title: Text — Dians tal
dialogs.intro: Saturday evening, after the main course. Jonas taps his glass and announces: "Och nu har vi kommit till talet från brudens bästa vän, Dian." Dian stands up. This is her speech.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Kära Elin, kära Erik, kära familj och vänner.
lines.id: Dear Elin, dear Erik, dear family and friends.
lines.literal: dear Elin, dear Erik, dear family and friends.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: För fem år sedan kom jag till Sverige med två resväskor och fyra svenska ord: hej, tack, fika och IKEA.
lines.id: Five years ago I came to Sweden with two suitcases and four Swedish words: hej, tack, fika and IKEA.
lines.literal: for five years since came I to Sweden with two suitcases and four Swedish words…

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Den första som förstod min svenska var Elin. Eller — hon låtsades i alla fall väldigt övertygande.
lines.id: The first person who understood my Swedish was Elin. Or — at any rate she pretended very convincingly.
lines.literal: the first who understood my Swedish was Elin. or — she pretended in all cases very convincingly.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Hon lärde mig att man ber om ursäkt när någon annan krockar med en, och att den sista kakbiten på fatet heter skambiten och att ingen tar den.
lines.id: She taught me that you apologize when somebody else bumps into you, and that the last cookie on the plate is called "the shame piece" and that nobody takes it.
lines.literal: she taught me that one asks for excuse when someone else collides with one, and that the last cookie-piece on plate-the is-called shame-piece-the and that nobody takes it.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Hon lärde mig också vad lagom betyder. Det tog bara tre år.
lines.id: She also taught me what lagom means. It only took three years.
lines.literal: she taught me also what lagom means. it took only three years.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Erik, jag ska vara ärlig. När jag träffade dig första gången tänkte jag: han är inte helt hopplös.
lines.id: Erik, I'll be honest. When I met you the first time I thought: he's not completely hopeless.
lines.literal: Erik, I shall be honest. when I met you first time-the thought I: he is not wholly hopeless.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Och i det här landet är det, som ni vet, den finaste komplimang man kan få.
lines.id: And in this country, as you know, that's the finest compliment you can get.
lines.literal: and in this here country-the is it, as you-all know, the finest compliment one can get.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Ni två har något ganska ovanligt: ni kan vara tysta tillsammans utan att någon av er blir nervös.
lines.id: You two have something quite rare: you can be quiet together without either of you getting nervous.
lines.literal: you-two two have something rather unusual: you can be quiet together without that any of you becomes nervous.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Ni diskuterar visserligen fortfarande vem som ska tömma diskmaskinen, men det är väl det som kallas kärlek.
lines.id: Admittedly you still argue about who's going to empty the dishwasher, but I suppose that's what they call love.
lines.literal: you discuss admittedly still who that shall empty dishwasher-the, but it is surely that which is-called love.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Om jag hade vetat för fem år sedan hur mycket ni skulle betyda för mig, hade jag lärt mig svenska ännu fortare.
lines.id: If I'd known five years ago how much you would come to mean to me, I'd have learned Swedish even faster.
lines.literal: if I had known … how much you would mean for me, had I learned me Swedish even faster.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Tack för att ni gjorde ett främmande land till ett hem.
lines.id: Thank you for turning a foreign country into a home.
lines.literal: thanks for that you made a foreign country to a home.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Får jag be alla att resa sig och höja glasen? Skål för brudparet!
lines.id: May I ask everyone to stand up and raise their glasses? To the bride and groom!
lines.literal: may I ask all to raise themselves and lift glasses-the? toast for bride-couple-the!

lines.speaker: Gästerna:
lines.text: Skål!
lines.id: Cheers!
lines.literal: bowl!

notes: **Kära Elin, kära Erik…** — *kär* (dear) takes the definite *-a* form in direct address: *kära vänner*, *kära familj*. Swedish speeches start with the couple, then everyone else; titles and long lists of guests are not expected.

**Hon låtsades** (**LOT-sah-des**) — *låtsas* is a deponent (Svenska 102, Unit 4): the *-s* form is active in meaning. Past *låtsades*, supine *låtsats*. Note that *någon annan krockar med **en*** uses *en* as the object form of *man* (Unit 6).

**Skambiten** (**SKAHM-bee-ten**), "the shame piece": the last biscuit or slice that nobody dares to take, because taking it seems greedy. Every Swede recognizes it, which is why it gets a laugh. The joke works through self-irony — Dian presents herself as the foreigner who had to learn it.
**Det tog bara tre år** — flat irony: *lagom* is famously easy to define and impossible to master. Pause before the line and say it without a smile.

**Om jag hade vetat …, hade jag lärt mig…** — an unreal condition about the past (Svenska 103, Unit 14). In the main clause *hade* + supine replaces *skulle ha* + supine and sounds more elegant in a speech. **Göra något till något** = to turn something into something.

**Skål för brudparet!** — *brudparet* (the bridal couple) is used for any couple, whatever their genders. The guests answer with one word, *Skål!*, then drink with the eye-contact ritual from the first dialogue.

grammars.title: The speech toolkit
body: A Swedish wedding speech is short (two to five minutes), personal and gently funny. This structure works for weddings, birthdays and farewell parties alike.

head: Step
Phrase
English
rows: *Jag heter … och har känt Elin sedan…*
My name is … and I've known Elin since…
I remember when… / Five years ago…
*Jag önskar er all lycka i världen.*
I wish you all the happiness in the world.
*Får jag be alla att höja glasen? Skål för…!*
May I ask everyone to raise their glasses? To…!

after: *Tack för att ni gjorde…* — after *tack för att* the clause keeps subordinate word order, and *inte* would come before the verb: *tack för att ni **inte** glömde mig*.
In speeches, Swedes often address the couple as *ni* and talk about them as *de* in the same speech. Keep each sentence clear about which one you mean.

blocks.text: Some Swedish wedding customs surprise foreign guests. The bride and groom often walk down the aisle **together**, instead of the father giving the bride away. At dinner, if the bride leaves the room, the women may line up to kiss the groom — and if the groom leaves, the men kiss the bride (on the cheek). And the evening is long: speeches between every course, songs from printed song sheets, dancing until late.

blocks.title: Giving a speech: five rules
items: Register your speech with the toastmaster beforehand.
Keep it short — three minutes is perfect.
Tell one story, not five.
Make fun of yourself, not of the couple.
End with a toast, and keep eye contact.

blocks.text: Dian's speech uses grammar from every level of this series. Read it once more and spot the pieces: that is how far you have come since *Hej, jag heter Dian*.

blocks.title: Where to go from here
items: **Read**: *8 Sidor* (easy news), then real newspapers; then Swedish novels — start with crime fiction, which uses everyday language.
**Listen**: *Klartext* on Sveriges Radio for easy news; podcasts and *SVT Play* with Swedish subtitles.
**Test yourself**: the *Tisus* exam proves the Swedish level required for university studies in Sweden.
**Speak**: join a *språkcafé* or a *förening* (club). Ask Swedes to switch from English back to Swedish: *Kan vi ta det på svenska?*

exercises.title: Series review
exercises.prompt: Translate into Swedish. Each sentence uses grammar from a different level.
items: When I came to Sweden, I didn't understand anything.
The house was built in 1890.
She said that she didn't have time.
If I had known, I would have come earlier.
Thank you for turning a foreign country into a home.
May I ask everyone to raise their glasses?

answers: glasen — brudparet — hem — hade — till — är
Han är inte helt hopplös. — Det har jag lärt mig av er. — Svenskar skrattar mest åt självironi. — Skämtet gick inte hem. — Ni kan vara tysta tillsammans.
Maten var inte så dum. — Erik är inte helt hopplös. — Talet var inte illa. — Konserten var inte så tokig. — Det kunde ha varit värre.

När jag kom till Sverige förstod jag ingenting. — Huset byggdes 1890. — Hon sa att hon inte hade tid. — Om jag hade vetat det hade jag kommit tidigare. — Tack för att ni gjorde ett främmande land till ett hem. — Får jag be alla att höja glasen?
